Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. I attached a marked-up MSA and Order Form (see attachments). Our legal team flagged two open points that are blocking signature:

1) Output ownership / title — ProspectCo needs explicit confirmation that we own outputs (customer data, generated text, and derivatives) produced using our inputs and configuration.
2) Model retraining / feedback license — we cannot grant an unlimited training license for our customer data/signals. We are open to limited usage for safety/quality, but need narrow carveouts and auditability.

High level asks: can Redwood accept (a) an explicit customer ownership clause for outputs, and (b) a bounded feedback/training license with purpose and retention limits?

We proposed language in the attached redline. If you can review and indicate which items are acceptable, we can try to move to DocuSign next week.

Appreciate the help — Janelle

Janelle — thanks for the redline and the clear summary. Attaching a short note and proposed tradeoffs our side can accept.

Quick take: we are comfortable with customer ownership of application-level outputs (customer prompts + generated output used directly by your product). We have concerns with a wholesale prohibition on using aggregate telemetry and non-identifiable feedback for model quality and safety improvements.

Proposed path:
- Output ownership: Agree to a clause that grants ProspectCo title to outputs generated from Customer Prompt Data and Customer Configuration, excluding any model weights or pre-existing model IP.
- Feedback / retrain license: Offer a limited license: Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated usage data and model outputs solely to improve service safety and quality, with a retention cap and an opt-out mechanism for specific data categories. No commercial model retraining that results in a new model variant trained exclusively on ProspectCo data without separate agreement.

I've looped in Rishi (legal) and Laura (sales/contracts) to draft precise clause language. Can you confirm whether ProspectCo needs any additional attribution or export controls (e.g., country restrictions) in the MSA?

Next steps: Rishi will propose clause text by tomorrow; Laura and I will prepare an Order Form with those limits included. If that looks good to you we can update the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Olga

Folks — drafting suggested clause text below. I kept it narrow and operational so sales can accept it without escalating to execs. Please advise if any commercial redlines are needed.

----- Suggested Clause: Customer Outputs and Use of Feedback -----
1. Customer Outputs. Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to outputs ("Customer Outputs") generated by the Service solely from Customer-provided input data, prompts, and Customer Configuration. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood retains ownership of its underlying models, model weights, and pre-existing model IP.

2. Feedback and Limited Use License. Customer hereby grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use de-identified and aggregated usage data ("Feedback") for the purpose of improving the performance, safety, and reliability of Redwood's services. Redwood shall not use Customer Feedback to train or fine-tune a model in a way that creates a product or model variant that is predominantly trained on Customer's proprietary data, unless a separate agreement is executed.

3. Retention and Audit Rights. Redwood will retain Feedback only for a period not to exceed eighteen (18) months for the stated purposes and shall provide Customer, upon reasonable request and subject to confidentiality protections, a summary of categories of Feedback used.

4. Opt-Out and Scope Limitations. Customer may notify Redwood in writing of specific data categories or datasets to be excluded from Feedback (e.g., legally protected data, certain PII categories). Upon receipt, Redwood will exclude such categories from any Feedback processing where reasonably practicable.

5. Exceptions for Safety. Notwithstanding section 2, Redwood may process limited Customer data for urgent security or safety incident response, subject to notification and minimal necessary scope.

If ProspectCo confirms the retention period (we proposed 18 months) and the opt-out mechanism, I think this is a commercially reasonable compromise.

Olga / Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the suggested language. ProspectCo legal reviewed. A few follow-ups / requested edits: 

- Output ownership: we can accept section 1 as written but need an explicit line that "Customer Outputs" includes derivative works created by ProspectCo from those outputs.
- Feedback license: the 18-month retention is acceptable, but we want a stricter limitation on purpose: "improving safety and security only" rather than general quality/feature improvements. We worry that "quality and performance" could be read to allow feature-building that duplicates our product.
- Opt-out mechanics: need SLA on responses (e.g., Redwood will confirm exclusion within 10 business days and cease processing within 30 days where feasible).

Also we are asking for one narrow commercial exception: ProspectCo requests that Redwood not use Feedback to create competing features that materially compete with ProspectCo's core product for 24 months after contract termination. We understand this is a big ask; if Redwood can't accept, please propose mitigations (e.g., longer notice, carveout fees, or explicit scope limits).

If you can incorporate those edits into a counter-redline we will re-review and aim to sign by end of next week.

Regards,
Janelle

Janelle — appreciate the clear feedback. Short replies to each point and next steps below.

- Derivative works: we can add explicit language confirming that Customer Outputs include derivative works created by ProspectCo based on those outputs.
- Purpose limitation: we will narrow "improving performance, safety, and reliability" to "improving safety and security" for Feedback used without a separate commercial agreement. For broader feature improvements that could create product functionality, Redwood will seek explicit consent or a separate commercial addendum.
- Opt-out SLA: we can commit to confirm receipt of opt-out requests within 10 business days and to make commercially reasonable efforts to cease processing within 30 days; we'll add "where reasonably practicable" language to account for technical constraints.
- Non-compete mitigation: Redwood cannot accept a stand-alone non-compete. Proposed mitigation: a 24-month restriction on using Customer Feedback to build directly competing core-product features, but limited to products substantially similar to ProspectCo's identified core offering and subject to negotiated carveouts. We'll document this as an explicit commercial exception that requires additional compensation; Laura will include a rate sheet option in the Order Form addendum.

Next steps: Rishi will produce a combined counter-redline reflecting the derivative line, narrowed purpose, SLA language, and the proposed commercial mitigation for the competition concern. Laura will produce an Order Form addendum with the optional paid protection. If ProspectCo can confirm agreement in principle we will generate an updated DocuSign packet (link below).

DocuSign (updated packet coming): https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/ProspectCo_OrderForm_v2
